section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Linear Transformation
section_1.content: Define a matrix as a function that transforms a vector. Visually represent a 2D grid being stretched/rotated by a matrix 'A'. Explain that v' = Av.
section_1.example: A 2D vector [1, 0] being rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise by matrix A.

section_2.title: The Concept of Composition
section_2.content: Introduce the idea of applying two transformations sequentially. If transformation A is applied after transformation B, the total effect is a single combined transformation C.
section_2.example: A 'Robot Arm' sequence: First, a Rotation matrix (B) turns the arm, then a Scaling matrix (A) extends it.

section_3.title: Deriving the Matrix Product
section_3.content: Show that the composition (A ∘ B)v = A(Bv). Through substitution, demonstrate that the result is equivalent to (AB)v. Emphasize that the matrix product AB is simply the 'combined instruction manual' for the two transformations.
section_3.example: Tracking a cat's movement: Matrix B rotates the cat's coordinate system, and Matrix A flips it; show how AB combines these into one single net-transformation matrix.

section_4.title: Visualizing Non-Commutativity
section_4.content: Use an animation to show that applying A then B is not the same as B then A. This explains why matrix multiplication AB ≠ BA.
section_4.example: A character performing a 'Jump' (Transformation A) then a 'Spin' (Transformation B) results in a different final position than 'Spin' then 'Jump'.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Reiterate that matrix multiplication is not just arithmetic—it is the functional composition of geometric transformations. This provides the foundation for computer graphics and robotics.
section_5.example: A 3D video game character: Matrix chains (Bone transformations) determine where the character's hand ends up in space.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
